limitations: Per-request bitrate and endpoint latency do not identify which network or proxy queue held data.
The CSV contains no packet-loss measurements.

source_findings: Established idle paths could immediately use STARTUP multiplier after resuming.
A healthy compressed ACK could remove the RTT drain and restore 288.5 Mbps from 75 Mbps.
The app-limited early return could suppress actual queue/loss exit from STARTUP.

change.idle_restart: Require an actual data-send gap of at least minRTT and an explicit transport-idle signal. Resume with at most the learned delivery-rate estimate; do not arm on sparse readiness estimates or brief producer gaps.
change.after_drain: Maintain the reduced effective pacing rate. Increase at most 25% in one packet round with at least minRTT of elapsed wall-clock time; idle time creates no accumulated credit.
change.capacity_model: Keep bandwidth sampler, windowed capacity estimate and existing profiles. Higher-capacity valid models can regain their rate; no fixed Mbps cap.
change.startup: Real queue/loss exit checks precede app-limited plateau filtering.
change.platforms: Same Go logic in Xray and Mihomo; software and Linux EDT read the effective PacingRate.

verification.controller_tests: Full controller suites and Xray HY2 passed; new regressions, cold readiness, brief-gap, higher-capacity, ACK-compression/clock, integer and migration cases passed.
verification.ablation: Removing each of the three hooks separately reproduced its intended regression; no compile failure was substituted.
verification.race: Both controller packages and Xray HY2 passed.
verification.isolated_end_to_end: Dual HY2 clients each transferred 4,200,000 bytes in both directions through software, EDT, short-RTT and non-FQ fallback. Namespace FQ drops zero.
